name: Juno Phase 2 Final Closure Ledger
authority: This ledger is the release closure source of truth. A green local checker proves local evidence only; external deployment, authenticated production smoke, Apple hardware, signing, and GitHub check-runs remain explicitly stated per requirement.

visualEvidence: Activity, Changes, Terminal, Tests, Preview, Agents, Git and PR tabs are wired to typed event state.
performanceEvidence: Remote event and terminal buffers are bounded; no fabricated count or exit-code fallback remains.
accessibilityEvidence: Native Code surfaces use Dynamic Type, accessible status labels, and 44pt controls.
deploymentEvidence: Code preview, remote, and runtime wiring checks pass; native package and app gates are wired in CI.
requirements.notes: The mobile Code surface consumes structured task, test, agent, diff, preview, Git, and approval data.

visualEvidence: Terminal cards show supplied exit codes and logs; Tests show structured pass/fail/skip data; Agents show typed topology and status.
performanceEvidence: Terminal output and remote event transport use bounded buffers and lazy detail expansion.
accessibilityEvidence: VoiceOver summaries expose command status, test status, agent roles, and copy/deep-link actions.
deploymentEvidence: Runtime wiring and native package gates are passing locally and represented in the native CI matrix.
requirements.notes: Known fake patterns such as hardcoded exit 0, fabricated test counts, and canned agent topology are absent from production Code runtime sources.

visualEvidence: Changed files, real diff hunks, authenticated preview diagnostics, branch/commit/PR state, and deep links are rendered from runtime data.
performanceEvidence: Diff and preview history are bounded and large details are loaded on demand.
accessibilityEvidence: Diff additions/deletions, screenshot alternative text, diagnostics, and PR links have accessible labels.
deploymentEvidence: Preview and remote source contracts pass and are covered by the native CI package/app gates.
requirements.notes: The source contracts reject missing remote state rather than manufacturing a completed preview or Git state.

visualEvidence: Approval UI displays exact redacted arguments, risk class, provenance, expiry, and explicit Allow/Deny actions.
performanceEvidence: Receipt consumption is atomic and bounded to one execution.
accessibilityEvidence: Approval cards expose modal semantics, focus order, risk labels, and high-contrast actions.
deploymentEvidence: Approval dispatch static gate and web/native tests are part of the release verification path.
requirements.notes: The shared approval broker remains the execution chokepoint for Code and connector actions.

visualEvidence: Current native design gates hold at type=0, motion=0, glass=0, targets=410; all 140 iPhone/iPad target-size violations were removed and the remaining macOS/shared baseline is explicitly ratcheted.
performanceEvidence: Native chrome uses bounded surfaces and the established token system; no unbounded polling was added.
accessibilityEvidence: The design gates enforce Dynamic Type, reduced motion, opaque content surfaces, and 44pt targets.
deploymentEvidence: Swift contract/design checks and unsigned iOS/macOS build gates are configured in native CI.
requirements.notes: Counts are current repository measurements, not a ratchet presented as a completed redesign. Simulator screenshots are local evidence; physical device semantics remain separately blocked.

visualEvidence: Responsive model picker and settings sections expose capability, pricing, usage, voice, memory, apps, and danger-zone states.
performanceEvidence: Catalog filtering is local and bounded across the registered model set; settings writes expose Saving/Saved/Failed state.
accessibilityEvidence: Model selection has radio semantics and settings controls have labels, roles, and scalable text.
deploymentEvidence: Canonical model validation and native/web settings paths are included in local and CI verification.
requirements.notes: Web and native surfaces consume the same canonical model and settings contracts.

visualEvidence: Voice overlay, waveform, transcript, in-call controls, camera/photo surfaces, attachment notices, and the real Mac Qwen anti-loop run are captured under docs/release/evidence/phase2-final/.
performanceEvidence: Relay context, transcript, history, and reconnect payloads are bounded; audio/video transport remains throttled, and microphone uplink is suppressed through assistant playback plus a 750 ms acoustic tail.
accessibilityEvidence: VoiceOver transcript output and explicit pending/unavailable/error notices are localized and surfaced.
deploymentEvidence: Qwen is the funded production default, relay verifier and authenticated Voice routes pass locally, and a real Mac hardware Qwen session produced one answer with no self-heard repetition during the post-playback open-mic window.
requirements.notes: Playback completion accounting, interruption-safe flushing, and the acoustic tail guard prevent the model from transcribing and answering its own speaker output. Camera and screen-share semantic hardware checks remain separate external blockers.

visualEvidence: Mobile Voice exposes Files independently of vision, preserves attachment notices, and does not silently drop pending or unavailable documents.
performanceEvidence: At most four attachment IDs and 24,000 context characters cross the Voice context boundary; queries and reconnect history are bounded.
accessibilityEvidence: Pending, unavailable, no-vision, and image-fetch failures use explicit localized notices rather than silent degradation.
deploymentEvidence: Owner scoping, exact attachment kinds, durable transcript persistence, relay context forwarding, and canonical production relay checks are covered by source regressions and package tests.
requirements.notes: Ready/degraded knowledge passages are used as actual provider context; queued/indexing/extracting/OCR states remain pending and unavailable states remain explicit. Library image clones retain kind and fetch bytes before sending.

integrationTests: xcrun simctl launch and AVCaptureSession semantic check
visualEvidence: Camera preview and capture pipeline are implemented; simulator camera buffers cannot prove physical capture semantics.
performanceEvidence: JPEG frame compression and frame-size bounds are covered by native tests.
accessibilityEvidence: Camera active announcement and flip control labels are implemented.
deploymentEvidence: Physical iOS camera permission and capture validation require Apple hardware and signed app execution.
requirements.blocker: BLOCKED_EXTERNALLY: Hardware camera capture requires a physical iOS device with an active AVCaptureSession video feed; the simulator cannot provide valid camera semantics.
requirements.notes: No locally achievable implementation gap is concealed by this state.

visualEvidence: Screen-share active indicator and frame broadcast code are implemented; simulator execution cannot establish system broadcast semantics.
performanceEvidence: ReplayKit sample-buffer throttling is covered by the native contract surface.
accessibilityEvidence: Broadcast status announcement is implemented.
deploymentEvidence: Physical display capture and signed ReplayKit permissions require Apple hardware and provisioning.
requirements.blocker: BLOCKED_EXTERNALLY: ReplayKit broadcast extensions and screen recording require a physical iOS device with active display buffers and signed system permissions.
requirements.notes: No locally achievable implementation gap is concealed by this state.

visualEvidence: Rich artifact previews, versions, exports, sandboxed documents, and refused unsafe markup are represented by the shared viewer.
performanceEvidence: Artifact markup and export verification apply explicit size, archive, and preview bounds.
accessibilityEvidence: Artifact viewer uses document landmarks, headings, code copy controls, and explicit failure text.
deploymentEvidence: Chat artifact verification and export checks are included in the release test and build path.
requirements.notes: Generated chat artifacts are verified before presentation; a single deterministic repair is allowed only when the repair is unambiguous.

visualEvidence: Verified/repaired blocks remain renderable; refused blocks are removed and a structured activity receipt is retained.
performanceEvidence: Repair is capped at one bounded deterministic pass and output size is capped.
accessibilityEvidence: Refusal and repair receipts are exposed as user-readable activity/status text.
deploymentEvidence: Route-level verification runs before persistence and presentation, including targeted revision refusal.
requirements.notes: The durable receipt records checked, accepted/refused, repair count, and problems without pretending an unrepairable artifact is valid.

visualEvidence: Project workspace, Work run states, Pinned navigation, artifacts, files, chats, and Code entry points are wired to durable data.
performanceEvidence: Project and Work lists are paginated/bounded; remote logs and artifacts are not unbounded host reads.
accessibilityEvidence: Project headings, status groups, action labels, and deep links are accessible in web and native surfaces.
deploymentEvidence: Cloud Work sandbox, generated contract, scheduler, runner, and web/native integration checks are release gates.
requirements.notes: Cloud Work explicitly excludes host filesystem tools; host-only serializers are barred from remote routes.

visualEvidence: Automation state and Work history have explicit queued, running, parked, completed, and failed representations.
performanceEvidence: Scheduler and trigger poller use leases, bounded batches, and idempotent execution keys.
accessibilityEvidence: Automation statuses and failure text are exposed as semantic labels in the Work surface.
deploymentEvidence: Runner and scheduler entry points are covered by the release test suite and deployment workflow.
requirements.notes: No timed cosmetic progress is used as durable execution evidence.

visualEvidence: Research plan, source discovery, evidence, claim audit, revision history, and final report states are durable UI concepts.
performanceEvidence: Worker leases, cursors, bounded source/claim counts, and one bounded citation repair pass are enforced.
accessibilityEvidence: Research timeline and citation state are represented with semantic status text and source locators.
deploymentEvidence: Worker entry point, migrations, and production process requirements are documented; PM2 execution remains a deployment check.
requirements.notes: The opt-in PostgreSQL inspector suite proves persisted graph projection and owner isolation without depending on an ambient developer database.

integrationTests: RESEARCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL PostgreSQL projection and owner-isolation test
visualEvidence: Claim support, contradiction, strength, source snapshots, and citation audit are available to the inspector projection.
performanceEvidence: Claim and passage projections are bounded and indexed by owner/message/run relationships.
accessibilityEvidence: Citation locators and validation states are textual and navigable rather than color-only.
deploymentEvidence: Database-backed projection test and research release suites are wired for CI with an explicit test database.
requirements.notes: Unsupported, partial, contradicted, and unverified claims remain labeled instead of being silently promoted.

visualEvidence: Memory receipt, source chat, category/lifecycle state, and Forget action are represented in the chat/settings surfaces.
performanceEvidence: Retrieval and consolidation use bounded context and explicit suppression/expiry rules.
accessibilityEvidence: Memory provenance and Forget controls have semantic labels and explicit confirmation/error state.
deploymentEvidence: Memory test and runner paths are part of the full Node and release verification suites.
requirements.notes: Automatic, natural-language, and manual writes share suppression and lifecycle gates.

visualEvidence: Untrusted provenance, requested permissions, consent, and approval states are visible in the action surfaces.
performanceEvidence: Skill scans and permission sets are bounded by manifest/version and tool schemas.
accessibilityEvidence: Trust, risk, consent, and refusal states have explicit text and accessible actions.
deploymentEvidence: Approval dispatch, skill trust, egress, and native extensibility checks run in release gates.
requirements.notes: Imported instructions remain untrusted content and cannot silently expand permissions.

visualEvidence: Auto-model selection and transparent fallback explanations are represented in chat model/status UI.
performanceEvidence: Local routing uses structured complexity/capability/plan signals without an LLM preflight.
accessibilityEvidence: Routed model and fallback notices are surfaced as semantic chat status text.
deploymentEvidence: Model validation, capability policy, provider health, and chat route selection are in release verification.
requirements.notes: Health-aware rerouting occurs at the chat selection boundary; auto selection remains deterministic and transparent.

visualEvidence: Model selector exposes the exact canonical Gemini 3.7 Flash identity and capabilities.
performanceEvidence: Catalog context window and capability metadata are explicit; no aliasing to 3.6 is used.
accessibilityEvidence: Model name, provider, capability, and availability are exposed in picker semantics.
deploymentEvidence: Model registry, native providerModelID, evaluator, and discovery migration tests all assert gemini-3.7-flash identity.
requirements.notes: The exact provider model ID is preserved through the Google route and native Code adapter; stale 3.7-to-3.6 claims are superseded by current source/tests.

visualEvidence: Provider degradation and fallback notices are typed and available to the chat/model surfaces.
performanceEvidence: Probe results are cached with TTL and failure classes; health checks use bounded one-token probes.
accessibilityEvidence: Health/fallback warnings are text-based, dismissible, and not color-only.
deploymentEvidence: Health policy and provider selection tests run in the full release verifier; live vendor quota remains environment-dependent.
requirements.notes: Authentication/billing failures are not treated as transient weather and are not hidden by fallback.

visualEvidence: Auth, refusal, trust, and failure states have explicit UI/status representations.
performanceEvidence: Crypto, ownership, DLP, CSRF/origin, and trust checks are bounded at their chokepoints.
accessibilityEvidence: Auth failure and security refusal surfaces use semantic messages and landmarks.
deploymentEvidence: Security regression suites and documented scope are required in the release verification workflow.
requirements.notes: Security review is scoped to web/API, relay, Work/agent trust, native auth, cryptography, and external connector boundaries.

visualEvidence: In-app Browser DOM and screenshots inspected public landing and sign-in surfaces; browser journey covers authenticated navigation/state assertions.
performanceEvidence: SSE completion/remount, reload, history, and bounded provider-failure journeys complete without timeout or polling hacks.
accessibilityEvidence: Public UI smoke covers semantic main/auth landmarks and the browser suite asserts visible labels and errors.
deploymentEvidence: Exact-SHA CI workflow installs browsers, seeds a disposable database, runs the verifier, and aggregates native/deploy checks.
requirements.notes: Local browser evidence uses the deterministic non-production smoke provider; authenticated production replay remains a separately controlled external check.

e2e: Authenticated production browser and HTTP smoke after deployment
visualEvidence: Local public landing/sign-in DOM and screenshots are captured; the production authenticated account is not available in this environment.
performanceEvidence: Smoke timeout and bounded receipt polling are explicit in the production gate.
accessibilityEvidence: Public production smoke includes auth-boundary and semantic landmark checks in the deploy workflow.
deploymentEvidence: Deploy workflow requires smoke credentials and a final deployed SHA before authenticated chat/receipt/replay smoke can pass.
requirements.blocker: BLOCKED_EXTERNALLY: The current environment has no production smoke base URL, controlled authenticated smoke cookie/token, or permission to create the required production receipt; local public Browser inspection cannot prove authenticated production health.
requirements.notes: The gate is intentionally blocked rather than converted into a health-only or unauthenticated claim.

e2e: Final deploy/native workflow runs for the pushed SHA
visualEvidence: Release evidence is recorded as machine-readable ledger/checker output rather than a dashboard screenshot.
performanceEvidence: CI wait has a bounded 45-minute aggregation timeout and uploads exact-SHA evidence.
accessibilityEvidence: CI failure output names the exact requirement/check that is red.
deploymentEvidence: Workflows check out github.sha, pass GITHUB_SHA, and aggregate named native/deploy checks; the final run must be attached after push.
requirements.blocker: BLOCKED_EXTERNALLY: A final exact-SHA GitHub Actions run cannot exist until the closure commits are pushed to origin/main; local verification cannot manufacture external check-run conclusions.
requirements.notes: This state is expected before the final push and must be changed to VERIFIED only after the exact final SHA workflows are green.

integrationTests: Physical iPhone/iPad install, camera, ReplayKit, APNs, and TestFlight execution
visualEvidence: Simulator builds and available simulator inspection provide non-physical UI evidence; they cannot prove device-only permission or sensor semantics.
performanceEvidence: Native package and app builds pass with warnings treated as errors where configured.
accessibilityEvidence: Native source contracts enforce Dynamic Type, reduced motion, and target-size checks.
deploymentEvidence: TestFlight distribution, Apple Developer ID notarization, and physical APNs/camera/screen-share validation require external Apple credentials, signing, and hardware.
requirements.blocker: BLOCKED_EXTERNALLY: Physical device/TestFlight execution and Apple notarization require an active paid Apple Developer Team, signing certificates, provisioning profiles, and available hardware.
requirements.notes: No simulator build or source gate is being presented as physical-device truth.
